definition: The main circuit board that connects and supports the processor, memory, storage, expansion cards, power supply, and other components.
The central processing unit that executes instructions and processes data.
Random-access memory stores data temporarily while programs are running.
A device that stores data and files for long-term use.
Provides electrical power to the internal parts of a desktop computer.
Removes heat from computer components and helps prevent overheating.
A circuit card that adds or improves computer functions.
A metal component that helps move heat away from the processor.
Material placed between the processor and cooling component to improve heat transfer.
Small supports that keep the motherboard from touching the computer case.
Clips that hold components securely in their sockets or slots.
A strap used to prevent electrostatic discharge when handling internal components.
A container used to organize and keep track of screws and parts during disassembly.
System software that manages computer hardware and provides a platform for other software.
Software that lets the operating system communicate with hardware devices.
Software that helps maintain or protect the computer system.
Low-level software built into a hardware device.
Software used to perform a specific task for a user.
The physical parts of a computer that can be seen and touched.
Instructions and programs that tell computer hardware what to do.
An external device connected to a computer.
An input device used to enter letters, numbers, symbols, and commands.
An output device that displays visual information.
An input device used to point, select, and move items on a computer screen.
